blocks.prompt:
1. Discuss the different complexity classes (P, NP, NP-hard, NP-complete) and their importance in understanding problem difficulty.
(Alag alag complexity classes (P, NP, NP-hard, NP-complete) aur masle ki mushkil samajhne mein un ki ahmiyat par baat kijiye.)
blocks.explanation:
Complexity classes maslon ko is hisaab se groups mein rakhti hain ke woh kitne mushkil hain aur kitna waqt lete hain.
1. Class P:
- Woh masle jo computer deterministic (tay qadamon wale) algorithm se polynomial time mein efficiently hal kar le.
- Input barhne par waqt qaabil-e-intezam raftaar se barhta hai.
- Misal: [4, 1, 3, 2, 5] ko [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] mein sort karna.
2. Class NP (Non-deterministic Polynomial time):
- Woh masle jin ka diya gaya hal jaldi check (verify) ho sakta hai, chahe hal dhoondna mushkil aur lamba ho.
- Misal: Sudoku: bhari hui 9 x 9 grid check karna aasan, khaali se hal karna mushkil.
3. NP-hard:
- NP ke sab se mushkil maslon jitne ya un se zyada mushkil; koi efficient algorithm maloom nahi.
- Misal: Travelling Salesman Problem: 5 cities ke 120 routes, 10 ke 3,628,800 aur 20 ke taqreeban 2.43 x 10^18.
4. NP-complete:
- Jo NP mein bhi hon aur NP ke sab se mushkil maslon jitne mushkil bhi. Agar ek NP-complete masla efficiently hal ho jaye to tamam NP masle ho jayenge.
- Misal: Knapsack problem: items ka diya gaya chunao check karna aasan, magar weight limit ke andar sab se qeemti combination dhoondna items barhne par bohat mushkil.
Rishta (Figure 3.4): P, NP ke andar hai; NP-complete NP aur NP-hard ka mushtarka (overlap) hissa hai.
Ahmiyat:
- Pata chalta hai ke masla efficiently hal ho sakta hai ya bare input par exact hal amli nahi.
- Tareeqa chunne mein madad: P maslon ke liye exact algorithm, NP-hard ke liye approximate ya heuristic tareeqe.
- Waqt aur resources bachte hain; "kya P = NP?" ka khula sawal cryptography aur algorithm design par asar rakhta hai.

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Aasan misal: Sudoku ka hal koi de de to check karna 1 minute ka kaam (NP: verify aasan), magar khud hal karna ghanton le sakta hai. Sorting jaisa kaam jaldi ho jata hai (P). TSP jaise masle mein shehar barhne par raaste itne barh jate hain ke computer bhi saalon laga de (NP-hard).

blocks.prompt:
2. Provide a detailed explanation of why the Halting Problem is considered unsolvable and its implications in computer science.
(Detail se samjhaiye ke Halting Problem unsolvable kyun hai aur computer science mein is ke implications (asar) kya hain.)
blocks.explanation:
Halting Problem poochta hai: koi bhi program aur us ka input diya ho, kya koi algorithm bata sakta hai ke program kabhi ruk (halt) jayega ya hamesha chalta rahega?
Unsolvable kyun:
- Alan Turing ne sabit kiya ke koi general algorithm tamam program-input pairs ke liye yeh jawab nahi de sakta. Masla unsolvable hai jab koi algorithm har soorat mein hal na de sake.
- Saboot ka khayal (contradiction se):
1. Farz karein algorithm halts(P, x) mojood hai jo hamesha sahi batata hai ke program P input x par rukega ya nahi.
2. Naya program Trouble(P) banayein: yeh halts(P, P) bulata hai; jawab "rukega" ho to Trouble hamesha chalta rahe; jawab "nahi rukega" ho to Trouble ruk jaye.
3. Ab Trouble ko khud apne aap par chalayein. Agar halts kahe Trouble rukega to Trouble hamesha chalega; agar kahe nahi rukega to Trouble ruk jayega.
4. Har jawab ghalat sabit hota hai, is liye aisa algorithm ho hi nahi sakta.
- Program chala kar dekhna bhi kaafi nahi: agar abhi tak nahi ruka to yaqeen nahi ho sakta ke baad mein nahi rukega.
Asraat (implications):
1. Computers ki bhi had hai: kuch saaf bayan kiye gaye masle koi algorithm kabhi hal nahi kar sakta.
2. Koi tool har infinite loop ya har bug yaqeeni taur par nahi pakar sakta; asal tools adhoore ya andaze wale jawab dete hain.
3. Masle par kaam se pehle check karein ke woh solvable hai, taake waqt aur resources bachein.
4. Is se maslon ki solvable aur unsolvable mein taqseem hui, jo computability theory ki bunyad hai.
(Saboot ka khaka chapter se aage hai; chapter sirf Turing ka natija batata hai.)

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Seedhi baat: koi aisa "jadoo ka program" nahi ban sakta jo har program dekh kar bata de ke woh kabhi rukega ya nahi. Agar banaya jaye to hum ek ulta program bana kar usay ghalat sabit kar sakte hain. Is liye compilers bhi har infinite loop nahi pakar sakte.

blocks.prompt:
3. Discuss the characteristics of search problems and compare the efficiency of Linear Search and Binary Search algorithm.
(Search problems ki characteristics par baat kijiye aur Linear Search aur Binary Search ki efficiency ko compare kijiye.)
blocks.explanation:
Search problem woh masla hai jis mein koi hal ya item dhoondna ho jo khaas shartein poori kare.
Khasusiyat:
- Input: data ka majmua (list, database, graph) aur target ya shart.
- Output: item ya us ki position, ya yeh ke item mojood nahi.
- Kai comparisons lag sakte hain; bare data par efficiency aham hai.
- Kuch tareeqon ko data khaas shakal mein chahiye (Binary Search ko sorted data).
- Information retrieval, database queries aur decision making mein istemal.
Linear Search aur Binary Search ka muqabla neeche table mein hai: bare sorted data par Binary Search bohat tez hai, jab ke Linear Search saada hai aur unsorted data par bhi chalti hai.
Program:
def linear_search(items, target):
    for i in range(len(items)):
        if items[i] == target:
            return i
    return -1

def binary_search(items, target):
    low, high = 0, len(items) - 1
    while low <= high:
        mid = (low + high) // 2
        if items[mid] == target:
            return mid
        elif target < items[mid]:
            high = mid - 1
        else:
            low = mid + 1
    return -1

cities = ["Karachi", "Lahore", "Islamabad", "Faisalabad"]
print(linear_search(cities, "Islamabad"))
print(binary_search([1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13], 7))
Output:
2
3

Darmiyani item check, phir sirf baayan ya daayan aadha; dohrao
Unsorted list par bhi chalti hai
Sirf sorted list par chalti hai
Time complexity O(n): worst case mein tamam n items check
Time complexity O(log n): har qadam par range aadhi
1,000,000 items: 1,000,000 tak comparisons
1,000,000 sorted items: sirf taqreeban 20 comparisons (2^20 taqreeban das lakh)

Misal: [1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13] mein 7 pehle hi check par

Bare sorted data par bohat tez

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Binary Search ko dictionary mein lafz dhoondne jaisa samjhein: beech se kholo, dekho lafz pehle hai ya baad mein, aur aadhi kitaab chhor do. Har dafa aadha kaam khatam, is liye das lakh mein bhi sirf ~20 qadam. Magar shart yeh hai ke data pehle se sorted ho.

blocks.prompt:
4. Discuss the nature of optimization problems and provide examples of their applications in real-world scenarios.
(Optimization problems ki nature (kis qisam ka hai) par baat kijiye aur asal zindagi mein un ke istemal ki misalein dijiye.)
blocks.explanation:
Optimization problem woh masla hai jis mein koi bhi nahi balke kisi meyaar (criteria) ke mutabiq sab se behtar hal dhoondna ho.
Nature (fitrat):
1. Bohat se mumkina (feasible) hal hote hain; unhein kisi paimane jaise kharcha, faasla, waqt ya qeemat se compare kiya jata hai jise kam (minimize) ya zyada (maximize) karna ho.
2. Hal ko constraints (hadood) poori karni hoti hain, maslan weight capacity ya budget.
3. Mumkina hal aksar bohat tezi se (factorial ya exponential) barhte hain, is liye kai optimization masle NP-hard hain aur bare input par exact hal nahi hote.
4. Inhein greedy algorithms, dynamic programming, divide and conquer, ya approximate/heuristic tareeqon se hal kiya jata hai; Generate and Test sahi hal to deta hai magar behtareen ki guarantee nahi.
Asal zindagi ki misalein:
- Travelling Salesman Problem / delivery routes: har shehar (ya customer) ko ek dafa ja kar wapas aane ka sab se chhota raasta; courier aur food delivery services.
- Route planning: do jagahon ke darmiyan sab se chhota ya tez raasta, jaise map apps (aur paanch colleges wali class activity).
- Knapsack problem: weight limit ke andar sab se qeemti cheezein chunna, maslan truck load karna ya budget ke andar projects chunna.
- Coin change: kam se kam sikkon mein raqam dena (greedy).
- Scheduling aur timetable: classes, exams ya kaam ko kam waqt aur resources mein tarteeb dena (chapter ki misalon se aage).

blocks.prompt:
5. Explain the Backtracking technique with reference to the N-Queens problem. Discuss how the algorithm explores different configurations to solve the problem.
(N-Queens problem ke hawale se Backtracking technique samjhaiye. Bataiye ke algorithm hal ke liye alag alag configurations kaise dekhta hai.)
blocks.explanation:
Backtracking hal ko qadam ba qadam banata hai. Agar koi adhoora raasta hal tak nahi le jata to algorithm pichhle qadam par wapas ja kar doosri choice aazmata hai, jaise ghalat sarak par mur kar doosra raasta lena. Yeh puzzles aur kai combinations wale maslon mein kaam aata hai.
N-Queens problem (chapter se aage; chapter sirf backtracking batata hai): N x N chessboard par N queens aise rakhni hain ke koi do queens aik doosre par hamla na karein, yani koi do ek row, column ya diagonal mein na hon.
Backtracking configurations kaise dekhta hai:
1. Queens ek ek row mein rakho, row 1 se shuru.
2. Mojooda row mein baayein se daayein columns aazmao; pehle safe column (oopar ki kisi queen ke column ya diagonal mein nahi) mein queen rakho.
3. Agli row par jao aur dohrao.
4. Agar row mein koi column safe nahi, to backtrack: pichhli row ki queen utha kar us ke agle safe column mein rakho.
5. Jab tak N queens rakh na di jayen (hal) ya tamam configurations aazma na li jayen, jaari rakho.
Misal (4-Queens):
- Row 1: column 1. Row 2: column 3 (1 aur 2 par hamla). Row 3: koi safe column nahi, backtrack.
- Row 2 column 4 par; row 3: column 2; row 4: koi safe nahi, phir backtrack. Row 3 ka koi aur safe column nahi aur row 2 ke columns khatam, is liye row 1 par wapas.
- Row 1: column 2. Row 2: column 4. Row 3: column 1. Row 4: column 3. Chaaron queens rakh di gayin.
Hal:
. Q . .
. . . Q
Q . . .
. . Q .
Program:
def is_safe(queens, row, col):
    for r, c in enumerate(queens):
        if c == col or abs(c - col) == row - r:
            return False
    return True

def solve(queens, n):
    row = len(queens)
    if row == n:
        return True
    for col in range(n):
        if is_safe(queens, row, col):
            queens.append(col)
            if solve(queens, n):
                return True
            queens.pop()          # backtrack
    return False

queens = []
solve(queens, 4)
print("Queen columns (row 1 to 4):", [c + 1 for c in queens])
Output: Queen columns (row 1 to 4): [2, 4, 1, 3]
Backtracking adhoori configuration ko qaida tootte hi chhor deta hai, is liye har mukammal arrangement aazmana nahi parta (8 queens ke 92 hal bina tamam placements aazmaye mil jate hain).

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Backtracking ko bhool bhulaiyan (maze) jaisa samjhein: ek raasta chuno, band gali aaye to pichhle mor par wapas aa kar agla raasta lo. N-Queens mein "band gali" woh row hai jahan koi bhi column safe na ho; wahan se ek row peeche ja kar queen ko agle column mein khiskate hain.

blocks.prompt:
6. Explain the process and time complexity of the Bubble Sort algorithm. Compare it with another sorting algorithm of your choice in terms of efficiency.
(Bubble Sort algorithm ka process aur time complexity samjhaiye. Apni pasand ke kisi aur sorting algorithm se efficiency ko compare kijiye.)
blocks.explanation:
Bubble Sort sab se saada sorting algorithms mein se hai. Yeh list mein baar baar chalta hai, saath wale (adjacent) elements compare karta hai aur ghalat tarteeb hon to swap karta hai.
Process:
1. List ke shuru se chalo.
2. Har saath wale jore ko compare karo.
3. Ghalat tarteeb ho to swap karo.
4. Passes dohrao jab tak koi swap baqi na rahe.
Har pass ke baad sab se bara baqi element bulbule (bubble) ki tarah aakhir mein apni jagah pohanch jata hai.
Misal: [5, 3, 8, 4, 2]
Pass 1: [3, 5, 4, 2, 8]
Pass 2: [3, 4, 2, 5, 8]
Pass 3: [3, 2, 4, 5, 8]
Pass 4: [2, 3, 4, 5, 8]
Program:
def bubble_sort(data):
    n = len(data)
    for i in range(n - 1):
        for j in range(n - 1 - i):
            if data[j] > data[j + 1]:
                data[j], data[j + 1] = data[j + 1], data[j]
    return data

print(bubble_sort([5, 3, 8, 4, 2]))
Output: [2, 3, 4, 5, 8]
Time complexity: O(n²), kyunke n items ke liye taqreeban n passes, har ek mein n tak comparisons. Input dugna ho to waqt taqreeban chaar guna. Samajhna aasan magar bare data ke liye inefficient.
Merge Sort se muqabla (neeche table): bare data ke liye Merge Sort zyada efficient hai; Bubble Sort sirf chhoti lists aur seekhne ke liye theek hai.

blocks.prompt:
7. Discuss the differences between time complexity and space complexity. How do they impact the choice of an algorithm for a specific problem?
(Time complexity aur space complexity ke farq par baat kijiye. Yeh kisi khaas masle ke liye algorithm ke choice (chunna) par kaise asar dalte hain?)
blocks.explanation:
Time complexity batati hai ke input barhne par chalne ka waqt kaise barhta hai; space complexity batati hai ke memory kaise barhti hai. Farq neeche table mein hain.
Algorithm ke chunao par asar:
1. Bare input ke liye kam time complexity: Bubble Sort O(n²) ki jagah Merge Sort O(n log n); sorted data par Linear Search O(n) ki jagah Binary Search O(log n).
2. Kam memory wale systems (chhote devices) ke liye kam space complexity: maslan gehre graphs mein DFS, BFS se kam memory leta hai.
3. Trade-off (len den): kuch algorithms waqt bachane ke liye zyada memory lete hain, maslan Dynamic Programming subproblems ke jawab store karta hai.
4. Masle ki zaroorat faisla karti hai: raftaar zaroori ho to tez algorithm, memory kam ho to kam memory wala; chhote data ke liye saada algorithm bhi kaafi.
5. Scalability: achhi time aur space complexity wala algorithm data barhne par bhi efficient rehta hai.
